Z:\repos\deps\claude-code-best-practice-shan\best-practice\claude-settings.md:362:### Per-Server Tool Loading (`alwaysLoad`, v2.1.121)
Z:\repos\deps\claude-code-best-practice-shan\best-practice\claude-settings.md:364:By default, MCP tool definitions are deferred (loaded into context on demand via tool search). Set `alwaysLoad: true` on an individual MCP server entry in `.mcp.json` (or inline `mcpServers`) to exempt that server from deferral — every tool from that server then loads upfront at session start regardless of `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH`. Available on all server types; requires Claude Code v2.1.121+. Use this only for a small set of tools needed every turn — each upfront tool consumes context that would otherwise be available for conversation.

91:**Key insight**: Nested skills are discovered **on-demand** when you work with files in those directories. They are not preloaded at session start.
92:
93:## Key Behavior: Description vs Full Content
94:
95:Skill descriptions are loaded into context so Claude knows what's available, but **full skill content only loads when invoked**. This is an important optimization:
96:
97:- **Descriptions**: Always in context (within character budget)
98:- **Full content**: Loaded on-demand when skill is invoked
99:
100:> Note: Subagents with preloaded skills work differently - the full skill content is injected at startup.
101:
102:## Priority Order (When Skills Share Names)
103:
104:When skills share the same name across levels, higher-priority locations win:
105:
106:| Priority | Location | Scope |
107:|----------|----------|-------|
108:| 1 (highest) | Enterprise | Organization-wide |
109:| 2 | Personal (`~/.claude/skills/`) | All your projects |
110:| 3 (lowest) | Project (`.claude/skills/`) | This project only |
111:
112:Plugin skills use a `plugin-name:skill-name` namespace, so they cannot conflict with other levels.
113:
114:## Why This Design Works for Monorepos
115:
116:- **Package-specific skills stay isolated** - Frontend developers working in `packages/frontend/` get frontend-specific skills without backend skills cluttering context.
117:
118:- **Automatic discovery reduces configuration** - No need to explicitly register package-level skills; they're discovered when you work in those directories.
119:
120:- **Context is optimized** - Only skill descriptions load initially, and nested skills are discovered on-demand.
121:
122:- **Teams can maintain their own skills** - Each package team can define skills specific to their domain without coordinating with other teams.
123:
124:## Character Budget Considerations
125:
126:Skill descriptions are loaded into context up to a character budget (default 15,000 characters). In large monorepos with many packages and skills, you may hit this limit.
127:
128:- Run `/context` to check for warnings about excluded skills
129:- Set `SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET` environment variable to increase the limit
130:
131:## Best Practices
132:
133:1. **Put shared workflows in root `.claude/skills/`** - Repository-wide conventions, commit workflows, and shared patterns.
134:
135:2. **Put package-specific skills in package `.claude/skills/`** - Framework-specific patterns, component conventions, testing utilities unique to that package.
136:
137:3. **Use `disable-model-invocation: true` for dangerous skills** - Deployment or destructive skills should require explicit user invocation.
138:
139:4. **Keep skill descriptions concise** - Descriptions are always in context (up to the character budget), so verbose descriptions waste context space.
140:
141:5. **Use namespacing in skill names** - Consider prefixing with package names (e.g., `frontend-review`, `backend-deploy`) to avoid confusion.
142:

362:### Per-Server Tool Loading (`alwaysLoad`, v2.1.121)
363:
364:By default, MCP tool definitions are deferred (loaded into context on demand via tool search). Set `alwaysLoad: true` on an individual MCP server entry in `.mcp.json` (or inline `mcpServers`) to exempt that server from deferral — every tool from that server then loads upfront at session start regardless of `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH`. Available on all server types; requires Claude Code v2.1.121+. Use this only for a small set of tools needed every turn — each upfront tool consumes context that would otherwise be available for conversation.
365:
366:```json
367:{
368:  "mcpServers": {
369:    "always-on-server": {
370:      "type": "http",
371:      "url": "https://mcp.example.com",
372:      "alwaysLoad": true
373:    }
374:  }
375:}
376:```
377:
378:An MCP server can also mark individual tools as always-loaded by including `"anthropic/alwaysLoad": true` in the tool's `_meta` object — useful when only a subset of a server's tools should bypass deferral.

36:## When to Use Each
37:
38:### Use an Agent when:
39:
40:- The task is **autonomous and multi-step** — the agent needs to explore, decide, and act without constant guidance
41:- You need **context isolation** — the work shouldn't pollute the main conversation window
42:- The agent needs **persistent memory** across sessions (e.g., a code reviewer that learns patterns)
43:- You want to **preload domain knowledge** via skills without cluttering the main context
44:- The task benefits from **running in the background** or in a **git worktree**
45:- You need **tool restrictions** or a **different permission mode** (e.g., `acceptEdits`, `plan`)
46:
47:**Example**: `weather-agent` — autonomously fetches weather data using its preloaded `weather-fetcher` skill, runs in a separate context with restricted tools.
48:
49:### Use a Command when:
50:
51:- You need a **user-initiated entry point** — a workflow the user explicitly triggers
52:- The workflow involves **orchestrating** other agents or skills
53:- You want to **keep context lean** — command content is not injected into the session context until the user triggers it
54:
55:**Example**: `weather-orchestrator` — the user triggers it, it asks for C/F preference, invokes the agent, then invokes the SVG skill.
56:
57:### Use a Skill when:
58:
59:- You want **Claude to auto-invoke** based on user intent — skill descriptions are injected into the session context for semantic matching
60:- The task is a **reusable procedure** that can be invoked from multiple places (commands, agents, or Claude itself)
61:- You need **agent preloading** — baking domain knowledge into a specific agent at startup
62:
63:**Example**: `weather-svg-creator` — Claude auto-invokes it when the user asks for a weather card; also callable from commands.
64:
65:---
145:### Auto-invocation
146:
147:| Mechanism | Can Claude auto-invoke? | How to prevent |
148:|-----------|------------------------|----------------|
149:| Agent | Yes — via `description` (use "PROACTIVELY" to encourage it) | Remove or soften the description |
150:| Command | No — always user-initiated via `/` | N/A |
151:| Skill | Yes — via `description` | Set `disable-model-invocation: true` |
152:
153:### Visibility in `/` menu
154:
155:| Mechanism | Appears in `/` menu? | How to hide |

193:## Layered architecture (shan canonical)
195:Per `Z:/repos/deps/claude-code-best-practice-shan/reports/claude-agent-command-skill.md` (2026-04-20):
207:Agents: autonomous + multi-step, own context, persistent memory, skills preload. Commands: orchestrate others. Skills: reusable procedures auto-fired on description-match.
292:Agents have ZERO parent context — briefs must be fully self-contained:
361:The "Agents have ZERO parent context" mandate at §"Agent Brief Template" above is **positive enumeration only** — it specifies what TO include in briefs. 155:    ### CR-12 disposition lattice (5 classes — Wave 134 Fire 27 series codification)
156:
157:    Beyond the **install-source priority order** (PRIMARY/SECONDARY/TERTIARY) above, every upstream-vs-incumbent relationship falls into ONE of 5 classes. Wave 134 Fire 27 series empirically mapped all 5:
158:
159:    1. **GENUINELY-NEW** — no Anthropic/incumbent parallel exists for the primitive's scope. Disposition: **INSTALL via CR-12 PRIMARY path** (official-native-channel per CR-6). No further audit needed beyond Probe DAG.
160:
161:    2. **DUPLICATE-FUNCTIONALITY** — full parallel exists in Anthropic/eee stack covering same scope and mechanism. Disposition: **REJECT-FOR-FIT** per `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/kiss-dry-yagni.md` Must-Never #4 (no duplicate functionality without clear reason).
162:
163:    3. **PARTIAL-OVERLAP** — incumbent and candidate cover overlapping function via DIFFERENT MECHANISMS. Disposition: **CASE-BY-CASE**, typically CITE-PATTERN-ONLY or STUDY-PILOT-PATTERN-EXTRACT. Example: Wave 134 Fire 27-C mem0 (fact-extraction-based memory) vs eee graphiti (temporal-KG-based) vs mcp-memory (sqlite-vec-based) — same memory layer, different mechanisms. Codex T1 verdict at `.claude/state/codex_consult_w134_f27c_mem0_OUT.txt` STUDY-PILOT-PATTERN-EXTRACT conf=0.87.
164:
165:    4. **PROVIDER-COMPLEMENT** — parallel API surfaces but different scopes; both can coexist. Disposition: **INSTALL as ALTERNATIVE (not PRIMARY)** — primary incumbent retains canonical position. Example: Wave 134 Fire 27-A openai-agents-python (vs Anthropic `claude-agent-sdk-python` @ HEAD `b512f256`) — Anthropic SDK = direct CC control plane (PRIMARY); OpenAI SDK = provider-agnostic orchestration (ALTERNATIVE). Codex T1 verdict at `.claude/state/codex_consult_w134_f27a_openai_agents_python_OUT.txt` STUDY-PILOT-PATTERN-EXTRACT conf=0.89.
166:
167:    5. **ECOSYSTEM-IMPORT** — core primitive GENUINELY-NEW at the surface level but imports parallel ecosystem at the dependency level. Disposition: **EVALUATE ecosystem cost vs core primitive value** (often CITE-PATTERN-ONLY when ecosystem footprint disproportionate). Example: Wave 134 Fire 27-B langgraph (Pregel BSP graph execution is novel BUT requires `langchain-core>=1.4.0a2` + 6+ langgraph-* sub-package import + LangSmith proprietary recommended). Pattern B HNF disposition at `.claude/state/codex_consult_w134_f27b_langgraph_OUT.txt`.
168:
169:    6. **CITE-CLASS-CANONICAL** — Anthropic-OFFICIAL educational/reference material (cookbook notebook / official docs / non-runtime / non-install artifact) ALREADY operating as TIER-1 cite reference per existing pin in `research-protocol.md` or equivalent. Distinct from PROVIDER-COMPLEMENT (parallel runtime mechanism) and ECOSYSTEM-IMPORT (core primitive new with ecosystem footprint) by requiring: (a) audited object is REFERENCE material not runtime/install artifact, (b) cite-class adoption is the CORRECT primary mode, (c) correct disposition is RATIFICATION of an existing eee rule/practice against the TIER-1-OFFICIAL primary source. Disposition: **ACCEPT-AS-CITE-REFERENCE** — do NOT install as runtime artifact; ratify existing eee discipline against TIER-1-OFFICIAL primary source; document operational-overlap for future cite-extraction priority queue. Empirical evidence: W152-F20 + F22 + F23 + F24 (n=4 same-arc 2026-05-11) — Anthropic Cookbook overall (F20 commit `4170fbc`) + CMA prompt-versioning ratified FM-21 OWNED rule (F22 commit `4ed6666`) + CMA human-in-loop ratified CR-7 + safety floor (F23 commit `04b1eb4`) + research-agent recipe ratified sota-researcher + multi-source-discovery-breadth (F24 commit `1d35a22`). **Promotion gate**: n=4 same-arc exceeds `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/codification-threshold.md:34-39,76-80` default n=2 confirmation bar (per cycle-321 expected-savings fast-path: ~3-10 min/audit × ~10-20 educational-source audits/month = ~30-200 min/month savings; LOC ≤200 fit).

174:    - When auditing ANY upstream candidate for eee adoption, FIRST classify per 6-class lattice (after Probe DAG passes); THEN apply class-specific disposition
175:    - Class assignment is determined by **mechanism comparison** vs incumbent (not surface API similarity alone)

Use this skill for anything in the software delivery lifecycle: writing a PRD ('write a PRD for X', 'let's plan X', 'scope this out'), parsing a PRD into an epic, decomposing an epic into tasks, syncing to GitHub ('sync the X epic', 'push tasks to github'), starting work on an issue ('start working on issue N', 'let's work on issue N'), analyzing parallel work streams, running standups ('standup', 'run the standup'), checking status ('what's next', 'what's blocked', 'what are we working on'), closing issues, or merging an epic. Do NOT use for: debugging code, writing tests, reviewing PRs, or raw GitHub issue/PR operations with no delivery context."

Every line of code has ongoing maintenance cost \\u2014 bugs to fix, dependencies to update, security patches to apply, and new engineers to onboard. Deprecation is the discipline of removing code that no longer earns its keep, and migration is the process of moving users safely from the old to the new.\\n\\nMost engineering organizations are good at building things. The value of code is the functionality it provides, not the code itself. When the same functionality can be provided with less code, less complexity, or better abstractions \\u2014 the old code should go.\\n\\n### Hyrum's Law Makes Removal Hard\\n\\nWith enough users, every observable behavior becomes depended on \\u2014 including bugs, timing quirks, and undocumented side effects. Does this system still provide unique value?\\n   \\u2192 If yes, maintain it. If no, proceed.\\n\\n2. How many users/consumers depend on it?\\n   \\u2192 Quantify the migration scope.\\n\\n3. Does a replacement exist?\\n   \\u2192 If no, build the replacement first. Don't deprecate without an alternative.\\n\\n4. What's the migration cost for each consumer?\\n   \\u2192 If trivially automated, do it. If manual and high-effort, weigh against maintenance cost.\\n\\n5. What's the ongoing maintenance cost of NOT deprecating?\\n   \\u2192 Security risk, engineer time, opportunity cost of complexity.\\n```\\n\\n## Compulsory vs Advisory Deprecation\\n\\n| Type | When to Use | Mechanism |\", \"numLines\": 60, \"startLine\": 1, \"totalLines\": 207}}"}
